recentItems.title: Xi urges diplomacy on Iran as Oman’s sultan makes historic visit to China
recentItems.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping says the Middle East should not become a “battleground for great-power rivalry”. 
He made the statement as he welcomed the Sultan of Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq to Beijing for a two-day state visit. 
Xi says China is willing to work with Arab nations to “achieve lasting peace”. 

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu reports from Beijing, China.

recentItems.title: After Israel’s election: What’s next? | The Bottom Line
recentItems.description:
The success of Palestinian-led parties – who won 15% of the vote in Israel’s elections – has created a conundrum for Israel’s leadership: partner with non-Zionists or accept political gridlock.

While the bloc led by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu got the most support from Israeli voters, it didn’t win enough seats in Israel’s parliament (Knesset) to build a ruling coalition so far.

Israeli politician Ofer Cassif, a member of one of the Palestinian-led parties, tells host Steve Clemons that the Israeli people “need to understand that the future must be a future of Jewish-Palestinian partnership and not another form of exclusion.”

recentItems.title: Bangladesh garment workers protest for higher wages as hundreds of factories shut
recentItems.description:
Thousands of garment workers have taken to the streets in Dhaka, Bangladesh, demanding higher wages as rising inflation puts pressure on household budgets.

Protests have led to clashes with police, the deployment of border guards and the temporary shutdown of more than 500 factories.

In a live report from Dhaka, Al Jazeera correspondent Tanvir Chowdhury describes the unrest. Human rights lawyer Taqbir Huda discusses why workers say the government's wage board has failed to account for rising living costs, and examines the role of Western fast-fashion brands in driving down production prices and putting pressure on workers.

Al Jazeera’s Tanvir Chowdhury reports from Dhaka.
